title: Hidden orchard
notes: Keep one adult at each table; an adult may hold the origin while the child chooses targets. On return, K-1 can compare blocker counts (P3), rows (P4), or first-dot hiding power (P5). Grades 2-3 can group dots by direction (P4), then use the number-rule and infinite-row questions (P5-6). Grades 4-5 can explain both directions of the criterion (P3-4), complete ray groups (P5), or justify exact blocker counts (P6-7). Saved sight lines should pass through dot centers; thread thickness is not a mathematical blocker.
